# EtymEx

> EtymEx traces where words come from. Each word page follows a word back through the languages it passed through (for example Latin → Old French → Middle English), with a lineage tree, a short narrative of how its meaning shifted, and the sources behind each step.

## Word pages

Every traced word has a page at `https://etymex.com/word/{word}`. Italian, Spanish, French and Portuguese words (beta) live at `https://etymex.com/word/{language}/{word}`, where `{language}` is `it`, `es`, `fr` or `pt`.

- [nice](https://etymex.com/word/nice): from Latin nescius, "not knowing"; once meant foolish
- [villain](https://etymex.com/word/villain): from Late Latin villanus, a farm worker
- [muscle](https://etymex.com/word/muscle): from Latin musculus, "little mouse"
- [window](https://etymex.com/word/window): from Old Norse vindauga, "wind-eye"

Every traced word is listed A to Z on the [index](https://etymex.com/words) and in the [sitemap](https://etymex.com/sitemap.xml).

## How entries are built

Each entry is synthesized from Etymonline, Wiktionary and dictionary sources. Every step in a lineage is marked with how well the sources support it, and reconstructed forms (such as Proto-Indo-European roots) are labelled as reconstructed rather than attested.

## Guides

- [FAQ](https://etymex.com/faq): common questions about etymology and how to use EtymEx
